summary: Georgian Bay light on Castle Bluff, Flowerpot Island, lit 1897; steel tower of 1968; volunteer-hosted in Fathom Five National Marine Park.

lens.note: seventh-order fixed white dioptric light in 1897

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed. Passenger ferry service from early May to mid-October, with tours from Tobermory. A museum occupies one keeper's dwelling.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (owner); site managed by the Friends of the Bruce District Parks Association (LighthouseFriends)

events.note: Square wooden lighthouse on Castle Bluff, north-east point of Flowerpot Island
Fixed white dioptric light of the seventh order at 88 ft above the water, in service in late autumn 1897
Two-storey keeper's dwelling built (LighthouseFriends dates it to 1900; the heritage statement dates it to 1901)
Fog bell moved to a detached platform at the opening of navigation; disabled August 1902 and later restored
LighthouseFriends dates the fog-alarm building to 1908. The 1909-10 report (fiscal year ended March 1910) says a fog-alarm was established at this light station. The two sources disagree on the date.
Pyramidal steel tower put in place
Old lighthouse burned and pushed over the cliff
Restoration work begun under an agreement between the Friends of Fathom Five and the Coast Guard
Red and white dayboards replaced the all-white dayboards

corrections.why: The record gives the steel tower as built 1969. LighthouseFriends says the pyramidal steel tower was put in place in 1968 and that the old lighthouse was burned the following year (1969). The Lighthouse Directory gives 1968. The record's events list already has 1968.

corrections.proposed: Canadian Coast Guard (owner); site managed by the Friends of the Bruce District Parks Association
corrections.why: LighthouseFriends says the Canadian Coast Guard owns the lighthouse and that the site is managed by the Friends of the Bruce District Parks Association. The Lighthouse Directory's entry for the light does not name Parks Canada as site manager; Parks Canada is not named for this light in the sources read, so it is removed from the proposal.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends dates the two-storey keeper's dwelling to the summer of 1900 (day labour, $1,397). The heritage register and the Lighthouse Directory date the principal keeper's house to 1901. The sources read do not settle which is right.
The record's 1969 tower date is the year the old lighthouse was burned after the 1968 steel tower went up (LighthouseFriends). The Lighthouse Directory gives the tower as 1968.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-27 (independent pass). (1) Fog bell, 1902-03: the 1903-04 report (fiscal year ended 30 June 1904) says the bell 'was again put in operation in September'. Read against its fiscal year, that September is September 1903. LighthouseFriends puts the return about a month after the August 1902 breakdown, which means September 1902. The sources disagree by a year; the story says so. (2) Fog alarm: the 1909-10 report (fiscal year ended March 1910) says 'a fog-alarm was established', with the diaphone plant bought for $2,400 and the building costing $2,010.65. LighthouseFriends dates the building to 1908. The story now states the conflict. The record's 1908 event stays, with a note. (3) Keepers matched by column position on the page images: Currie (1906-07, printed p.163, scan 172; appointed 18 August 1904 at $300) and D. Smith (1911-12, printed p.247, scan 254; appointed 6 October 1909 at $260) are both confirmed. The Lamb Island entries on the same 1911-12 page are confirmed too. (4) LighthouseFriends roster after 1950 (Coultis, Freethy, Spears's line) is printed as the roster gives it; Audrey Coultis (1950-1982) and John Freethy (1982-1987) connect with the station after about 1960 and are named only as LighthouseFriends prints them. The lightning-strike account involving a keeper's family is left out. (5) Athabasca: LighthouseFriends says the crew blamed the keeper because the foghorn was not sounding, and Keeper Daniel Smith blamed the crew. The story gives both, attributed to LighthouseFriends, which cites two Buffalo Evening News articles (19 October and 19 November 1909) that were not read. (6) Marion L. Breck (mid-October 1900) and the Smith rescue rest on LighthouseFriends alone; no departmental report or newspaper was read. The departmental reports before 1900 are not in the corpus. (7) Site management: LighthouseFriends names the Coast Guard as owner and the Friends of the Bruce District Parks Association as site manager. Parks Canada is removed from the story and from the agency field, because no source read ties it to this light. Fathom Five National Marine Park is cited to LighthouseFriends and the register. (8) Units: the story now gives metres first (26.8 m (88 ft) for the 1897 light height). Quoted feet stay inside quotations. (9) Directory of Federal Heritage Designations: not used.
